title: Understanding and Predicting Cross-Application I/O Interference in HPC Storage Systems
problem: Multiple concurrent workloads in shared HPC storage systems compete for I/O resources, causing inter-application contention that degrades individual application performance. Prior work lacks quantitative frameworks to predict how I/O interference impacts application performance.
motivation: Accurate prediction of I/O interference enables more efficient resource provisioning and workload management strategies in shared HPC storage systems.
method: The framework watches each application's input/output operations in detail and simultaneously measures what the storage system is doing. It trains a machine learning model—a system that learns patterns from data—to understand how applications competing for the same storage resources interfere with each other. The trained model can then predict whether interference will occur and estimate how much each application's performance will suffer.
key_novelty: This method predicts how applications interfere with each other in shared HPC storage by tracking detailed I/O operations and using machine learning to find the patterns that cause slowdowns.
contributions: Framework for collecting fine-grained I/O traces and concurrent server-side metrics from HPC applications
Machine learning model achieving >90% F1 score for predicting I/O interference existence and quantitative impacts
Analysis of I/O interference dynamics on application I/O patterns and system status
Validation on both synthetic benchmarks and real-world HPC applications
primary_theme: Predicting cross-application I/O interference in HPC storage
